question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #13: A high-throughput transaction processing engine reported severe performance degradation under Object-Oriented & Functional Design Patterns. P99 latency increased from 15ms to 850ms, and telemetry indicates elevated CPU instruction stalls and thread contention during 'Functional Composition and Immutability' operations.

### Engineering Challenge:
As the Principal Software Engineer, what is the most technically rigorous root-cause remediation for this 'Functional Composition and Immutability' issue?

options.text: Increase the maximum thread pool limit by 4x and enable synchronous garbage collection passes.
Restructure the critical section in Functional Composition and Immutability to utilize lock-free atomic primitives or fine-grained partition keys, eliminating thread convoying.
Wrap the entire execution path in a global reentrant mutex to force strict serial execution.
Disable thread affinity pinning and disable all memory cache prefetching on host CPUs.

answer_explanation: Under high concurrency in Object-Oriented & Functional Design Patterns, thread contention on coarse-grained synchronization locks causes thread convoying and frequent context switching. Migrating to lock-free atomic operations or partitioned striped locks resolves the bottleneck without latency spikes.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option B. Rationale: Under high concurrency in Object-Oriented & Functional Design Patterns, thread contention on coarse-grained synchronization locks causes thread convoying and frequent context switching. Migrating to lock-free atomic operations or partitioned striped locks resolves the bottleneck without latency spikes.
